original_question: When information geometry is extended from static statistical problems to dynamics, what is the purely information-geometric and mathematically sound construction of the additional dual tangent-cotangent structure needed for velocities and forces?
target_in_paper: Section 3 (Tetsuya J. KOBAYASHI): "What would be the purely information geometric and mathematically sound construction for such a joint-structure for dynamics?" This is the exact open problem your draft is targeting. The immediately preceding sentence specifies that the sought object is "another metric or dually flat structure" on the dual pair of tangent and cotangent spaces for velocity and force, over a base manifold already equipped with the conventional dually flat structure. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's core intent very well: it correctly identifies the extension from static information geometry to dynamics, the need for extra structure beyond the usual static dually flat geometry, the tangent/cotangent interpretation in terms of velocity and force, and the demand that the construction be both purely information-geometric and mathematically sound. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
missing_details: The paper does not ask merely for an unspecified extra dual structure; it explicitly says the new object may be "another metric or dually flat structure." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The base object is a manifold already equipped with the conventional dually flat structure from static information geometry; that background structure should be stated explicitly. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The additional structure is sought on the dual pair of tangent and cotangent spaces specifically because these represent velocity and force driving the dynamics. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The motivating dynamic settings named in the paper are diffusion processes, optimal transport, Markov jump processes, and chemical reaction networks; including these keeps the question faithful to the paper's scope. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The paper frames the goal as a "joint-structure for dynamics," i.e., a dynamic structure added over the pre-existing static one, not a stand-alone reformulation of ordinary dually flat geometry. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

There are no paper-specific ambient fields, coordinate choices, dimensional hypotheses, operator definitions, homogeneity/degree restrictions, nilpotency conditions, or asymptotic quantifiers here; a faithful rewrite should leave those unspecified rather than inventing them. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The paper gives this as a direct open-ended construction problem, not as a numbered conjecture/theorem or as an equivalence with another formal statement. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
refined_question: Let M be a base manifold already equipped with the conventional dually flat structure of static information geometry. Motivated by diffusion processes, optimal transport, Markov jump processes, and chemical reaction networks, how can one construct, purely within information geometry and with full mathematical rigor, an additional dynamic joint-structure—namely, another metric or dually flat structure on the dual pair (T_xM, T_x^*M) encoding the velocity and force that drive dynamics on M? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
justification: This paper is a collection of open problems rather than a theorem/conjecture paper, and after the abstract it proceeds directly by speaker-labeled sections; there is no Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3 to target here. The nearest official formulation is therefore the final sentence of Section 3 by Tetsuya J. Kobayashi. The surrounding context in the same section is essential: it first recalls three standard constructions of dually flat structure for static information geometry, then states that work on diffusion processes, optimal transport, Markov jump processes, and chemical reaction networks suggests the need for another metric or dually flat structure on the dual tangent/cotangent pair for velocity and force, over a base manifold already carrying the conventional dually flat structure. Your draft is close, but it omits the explicit "another metric or dually flat structure" phrasing, the base-manifold-with-static-structure setup, and the motivating classes of dynamics. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
